notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. Sources are SAP's own PDF copies of the 2024 Annual Report on Form 20-F (filed with the SEC on February 27, 2025, accession 0001104659-25-017815) and the 2024 Integrated Report, both on sap.com; www.sec.gov was not contacted. Dividends, buybacks and stock comp are cross-checked against the SEC XBRL companyfacts API (CIK 0001000184). EUR, converted exactly from € millions. LEADER: Hasso Plattner, a cofounder, left the Supervisory Board on May 15, 2024. The 20-F major-shareholder table (as of February 7, 2025) covers 5% holders and current board members only and does not list him or his foundation or family vehicles, and the 20-F says parties related through him are no longer treated as related parties after May 15, 2024. No holding is reported, so status is 'no-reported-stake'. This does not mean he holds no SAP shares; the filing simply gives no figure. HOLDERS: percentages are '% of Outstanding' ordinary shares as reported to SAP. Dietmar Hopp's 5.1% rests on a Schedule 13G filed February 11, 2022, and BlackRock's 6.3% on a 13G filed February 2, 2024; asOf uses those filing dates because the 20-F gives no event dates. Dietmar Hopp is another SAP cofounder, not part of Plattner's holdings. BUYBACKS: €2,106 million 'Purchase of treasury shares' in the cash-flow statement, under the €5 billion programme announced May 16, 2023 (10,865,684 shares, about €2 billion in 2024). STOCK COMP: €2,385 million total share-based payment expense, of which €1,591 million equity-settled and €794 million cash-settled (Note B.3). Note B.3 adds that SAP 'additionally' recognised €309 million of accelerated share-based payment expense from its 2024 transformation programme, classified as restructuring expense; the wording indicates it is in addition to the recorded figure. GEOGRAPHY: the six country/sub-region rows; EMEA, Americas and APJ subtotals are not repeated.

footprint.notes: SAP publishes no U.S. state data. Country headcount is disclosed only for countries with 50+ employees and at least 10% of the total (Germany, United States, India) in the ESRS S1 section of the Integrated Report 2024; regions are FTEs from the 20-F (EMEA/Americas/APJ, which the filing defines by continent, not by country list). Tax: SAP publishes no country-by-country tax report; the 20-F splits current income tax expense into Germany (€418m) and foreign (€1,516m) for 2024. Cash income taxes paid (€2,277m net) are reported only for the group. Germany appears twice in countries because headcount and tax come from different documents. The 20-F also lists owned real estate in Newtown Square, Palo Alto and Colorado Springs (U.S.), Bangalore, Sao Leopoldo, London, Ra'anana and Sofia, and non-current assets by region (Germany €7,351m, U.S. €26,840m, India €405m), which were not recorded because they are dominated by goodwill.
